scope: Each mutation is considered separately over reachable healthy s3.5 states and canonical finite model action domains, including the one/two/five-page witness domains. The 38 individually configured model sweep faults and targeted fault continuations are tested, not universally proved equivalent. Constructor, domain and unused-call arguments are explicit; permission widenings use the healthy model's guarantee/order invariants. Reachability samples support arguments and are not exhaustive proofs. No old sampling receipt is relabeled as a current-source run.

H002.argument: Without typed input or risk, every held page has buf == base; NOPAGE does too. Init establishes this; submit sets typed, uncertain/conflict sets risk, Published/discard establish equality.
H002.review: rechecked against s3.5 source and constructor/transition call sites

H004.argument: Risk implies held. Every retirement installs NOPAGE, which is clean, so !held is redundant in clean-or-risk and risk predicates.

H020.argument: The locked page's promise cannot outrun its save job. An active same-version draft acknowledgement repeats bytes/ep; an active same-version saved acknowledgement repeats the saved record. Upgrade requires pr.on; an ended promise may retain different historical bytes, and is excluded. Each individual removal is either still rejected or repeats the original record.

H209.argument: At a healthy phase-2 save with guard true and bytes != base, the base is already seen or in opRead. Window input exposes its predecessor; CLI operations record the base they read, including ABSENT. Restore retains that provenance; a newly saved operation byte is initially clean, and a later meaningful edit either exposes it to a window or reads it through an operation. UNKNOWN mismatches cannot publish. writtenSeen is false in s3; removing both this exemption and the bytes!=base condition is not justified.

H302.argument: The Quint driver selects page arguments from PAGES, text arguments from TEXTS (plus ABSENT where permitted), keep/ref sets from subsets of PAGES, and complete TEXTS-valued maps for all refs. Thus the dropped domain check is true on every representable model input. Remaining canonical guard oracles use the same domains, including page counts 1, 2 and 5. This is unreachable invalid-input behavior, not equivalence for arbitrary Rust callers.

All gate updates only remove open members. A page with vers[q]==NONE is never in open, so removing q in that case is an identity. Gate pruning sees the same open set. A gate/obligation records the version installed by its operation. Every later page change advances that page's version; a save captures its current version. opFree forbids installing a new overlapping order during a save, touches forbids chaining over an existing order, and delivery/observe cannot change the saved page while locked. Thus a publishing save on an obligation's page has ver >= its installed version. Removing this comparison changes no retirement on a healthy reachable call. Consequently widening this conjunction also changes no healthy open set: a padding page is absent from open, and a publishing member's version comparison is already true.
